newsitem.title: INDIA: Hughes unit in $8.4 mln India VSAT deal.
newsitem.headline: Hughes unit in $8.4 mln India VSAT deal.

text.p: India's Hughes Escorts Communications Ltd (HECL) signed an $8.4 million deal with the Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) for 500 VSAT (very small aperture terminal) satellite earth stations on Friday.

At a news conference to sign the deal, DSE's president Deepak Chowdhry said: "The deal with HECL is for seven years. We are encouraging all our members to get VSATs so they can get as close to investors as possible, and don't have to come physically to the exchange to trade."

HECL is a joint venture between India's Escorts Ltd and Hughes Network Systems, a division of Hughes Electronics Corp, which is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp. It is the largest VSAT operator in India.
DSE has 375 members and all of them have cubicles at the exchange as remote telephone connections are not reliable.
Chowdhry said DSE will charge each member 100,000 rupees ($2,778) for a VSAT, and a monthly charge including airtime of 3,500 rupees.

"Going by the response of our members, where 70 VSATs were booked in a week, we expect to deploy at least 200 in a month's time," he said. Chowdhry stated that 500 VSATs could well be in use by July 1998, and a 1,000 in two years time.

DSE is the fourth stock exchange in the country to get VSATs, after the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the Bombay Stock Exchange and the Calcutta Stock Exchange. With over 1,000 VSATs, NSE has the largest number of VSATs of any bourse in the world.
